Information received since the March meeting points to a solid cyclical backdrop—strong job gains, low unemployment, inflation near 2 percent, and ongoing strength in business fixed investment—supporting the Committee’s gradual, data-dependent normalization under a symmetric 2 percent inflation goal. Market-based inflation compensation remains low, consistent with well-anchored expectations and a muted pass-through from tight labor markets in expectations-augmented/Sticky-Information frameworks.

Financial Stability Report insights temper the tone: while overall vulnerabilities are moderate, asset valuations appear elevated and corporate leverage has risen, even as near-term funding risks remain contained. These stability considerations reinforce credibility-preserving gradualism rather than an aggressive stance. Net tone: cautiously optimistic, with vigilance around pockets of vulnerability and continued monitoring of inflation expectations and financial conditions.
